claim: The head-arm amino alcohol: how many carbons?
locus_a: SI 'Materials' and 'Synthesis of AT1' both name 4-amino-1-butanol (4 carbons); the SI Experimental Method repeats it
locus_b: SI Schemes S4, S5 and S9 all DRAW the reagent as HO-CH2-CH2-CH2-NH2, three carbons (3-amino-1-propanol). Verified by counting bond vertices on the composited PNG at native resolution, not by eye on a thumbnail
what_we_emitted: FOUR carbons. Every emitted structure carries a 4-hydroxybutyl arm
why: Mass settles it and the margin is enormous. The two readings differ by one CH2, 14.0157 Da, on every one of the 39 lipids with a printed ESI-MS. The 4-carbon reading misses the SI's own printed [M+H]+ by at most 0.50 mDa -- which is the 3-decimal rounding floor -- while the 3-carbon reading misses by at least 14,015.32 mDa on its BEST case, a factor of 28,031. stage06 V7. The same class of defect as XD_2026's Fig 5A, where the paper drew ALC-0315 with a 3-carbon hydroxyalkyl head where the compound has 4

claim: Figure 1d versus Figure 1c: the same quantity, drawn twice
locus_a: Figure 1c, per-organ Avg Radiance for liver and spleen; spleen/liver computed from our reads
locus_b: Figure 1d, spleen-to-liver ratio drawn directly on its own axis; read independently with tick-anchored windows
what_we_emitted: Figure 1c only. Figure 1d is read as a CHECK and no value from it is emitted
why: The two agree at Spearman 0.993 / Pearson 0.996 over 26 comparable formulations, slope 1.015, median relative difference 4.7%, worst 26.7% (AT1-c-Bex, a short-bar pair). Figure 1d is larger in 18 of 26, which could mean it is the mean of per-animal ratios while 1c gives per-organ means -- those are not algebraically equal. TESTED: sign test p = 0.122, median ratio 1.015. NOT ESTABLISHED; the discrepancy is consistent with digitisation noise on short bars. Recorded with the measurement that failed to settle it rather than asserted

claim: Our Figure 1c shares versus Figure 2c's printed percentages
locus_b: Figure 2c prints spleen and liver percentages on five pie charts; renormalised to spleen+liver

claim: What the paper calls a 'scaffold' and what it calls a 'linker'
locus_a: Abstract, Introduction and Results 2.1: 'two molecular scaffolds (ATX-c-RA and ATX-RA), four linker motifs, and five retinoic-acid-derived hydrophobic domains'
locus_b: The four things called 'linker motifs' are AT1-AT4, and SI Scheme S3 shows they differ in the TAIL as well: AT1 is a C6 acid on pentadecan-8-ol, AT2 a C8 acid on heptadecan-9-ol, AT3 a C10 acid on heptadecan-9-ol, and AT4 is a 6-bromohexyl ester of 2-hexyldecanoic acid -- a REVERSED ester with a branched acid, not a linker-length variant at all
what_we_emitted: 2 x 4 x 5 = 40, emitted as 40 distinct structures. Our 01_blocks.csv calls the AT1-AT4 axis `atx_tail_motif` and the c/no-c axis `linker`, which is the opposite of the paper's words
why: Not a numeric contradiction and it changes no value -- the factorial is 2 x 4 x 5 = 40 either way, and it is PROVED in stage02 rather than restated. Recorded because a reader who takes 'four linker motifs' literally will expect AT1-AT4 to share a tail, and they do not; AT4 in particular cannot be described as a linker variant of AT1

claim: The Figure 1a colour scale has no units and no stated meaning
locus_a: Figure 1 caption: '(a) Luciferase expression in DC2.4 cells after 6 h incubation...'
locus_b: The colorbar is labelled only 1.0 / 0 / -1.0, with NO axis title, NO tick marks, and no statement anywhere in the article or the SI of what quantity has been scaled or how
what_we_emitted: Emitted, with the caveat on every row and DECISIONS.md D-2 left OPEN
why: Measured facts, not inference: the brightest cell's RGB equals the colorbar's top interior colour and the darkest equals its bottom, so the colour limits were set to the data's own min and max -- the scale is a min-max rescaling onto [-1,+1] of SOMETHING. Whether that something is log-scaled is what D-2 turns on, and the distribution test is inconclusive (panel a's 41 means have skew +0.10 and sit at 0.42 of range; this paper's own in-vivo values are at +0.7..+1.7 skew in linear units and -0.6..-1.2 in log10)

claim: Dlin-MC3 is formulated differently from the 40 RAILs
locus_a: SI: the commercial control is Dlin-MC3 50 / DSPC 10 / cholesterol 38.5 / PEG2k-C-DMG 1.5 mol%
locus_b: SI: the RAIL formulations fix the ionizable lipid at 33.3 mol% and scale the other three to the remaining 66.7
what_we_emitted: Two Formulation_IDs: KJ_2026_MC3control carries 50/10/38.5/1.5 and KJ_2026_RAIL carries 33.3/13.34/51.359/2.001
why: Not an error by the paper -- it says so plainly -- but it is a confound a reader of data_vitro.csv would not otherwise see: the benchmark in this experiment differs from the library in BOTH chemistry and molar composition, so a Dlin-MC3-versus-RAIL comparison from these rows is not a clean chemistry contrast. The control's four numbers are also Onpattro's published composition exactly (max |delta| 0.0 mol%), which the SI never says
